subject: JupiterAI — post-call growth plan & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@jupiterai.com>, Sasha Lee <sasha.lee@jupiterai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-18T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: JupiterAI — post-call growth plan & pilot next steps

Alex / Sasha — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

High-level pain points you described:
- Production RAG latency is spiking during peak query bursts (95th pctl > 600ms) which affects response SLAs for customer-facing search.
- Token costs have grown 35% month-over-month after moving more retrieval candidates into prompt context.
- Need for predictable throughput for a Q2 launch (expected 12k QPS peak across inference types).

Goals you confirmed:
1) Stabilize 95/99 latency under 350ms for search and 450ms for long chat sessions.
2) Reduce per-token inference cost by ~25% via batching/quantization without degrading generation quality.
3) Plan a staged migration from hosted to a Dedicated pool for high-volume customers by the end of Q2.

Proposed pilot (attached: jupiterai-pilot-scope-2026-01-18.pdf):
- 6-week Dedicated pilot: reserved pool sized for ~20% of projected Q2 peak with autoscale headroom.
- Evaluation metrics: 95/99 latency, tokens/sec per GPU, quality regressions on 500 prompt set.
- Deliverables: baseline perf run (week 1), quantization/kv-cache tuning (week 2–3), staged canary traffic (week 4–5), cutover checklist (week 6).

Next steps / owners:
- Redwood: schedule infra deep-dive with your infra/eng team (Ben) — proposed Wed 1/21 11a PT.
- JupiterAI: share representative tokenized prompt set and sample logs for last 30 days (Sasha) by 1/22.
- Procurement: early alignment on contract term and billing model (monthly reserved commit) — I’ll loop in Ben for pricing.

Please reply if this matches your understanding or if you want any adjustments. We’ll stand up the pilot plan once we have the sample dataset and confirm timing.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: JupiterAI — post-call growth plan & pilot next steps

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Confirmed on the pain points and goals. A couple of clarifying items: 
1) Our current peak numbers are bursty — the 12k QPS is an internal projection for the launch cohort; typical peaks today are closer to 5–7k. We can provide minute-level traces.
2) Quality: the search team is very sensitive to hallucination on long-context queries; when you say "quantization without degrading generation quality," can you outline expected regression thresholds and rollback mechanisms?

We’ll upload the anonymized prompt set and logs to the Drive link you shared by EOD 1/22. Procurement (procurement@jupiterai.com) will also ask for a preliminary SOW and committed pricing range so they can budget.

Alex — looping you for any scheduling preferences for the infra deep-dive.

Thanks,
Sasha Lee
Head of Platform Engineering, JupiterAI
Sasha.Lee@jupiterai.com | +1 (720) 555-0133

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-19T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: JupiterAI — post-call growth plan & pilot next steps

Looping in pricing and solutions context.
Jordan — I can support the Wed 1/21 11a PT deep-dive. For the quantization/regression question from Sasha: our approach is to run a two-arm evaluation during week 2–3 — FP16 baseline vs INT8/4 quantized run with a 500-prompt eval set plus automatic quality gates. If Rouge/EM-like proxies fall outside of agreed thresholds (we typically use <2% delta on top-k metrics or explicit manual checks), we auto-fail and revert to the baseline. We’ll include a rollback plan in the SOW.

I attached a draft pricing sheet for reserved capacity and burst credits (redwood-dedicated-pricing-terms-2026-01-24.xlsx will be finalized after the first data drop). For budgeting, we can show committed monthly pricing with a flexible step-up for additional capacity.

Ben Carter

Thanks all — Wed 1/21 11a PT works for the infra deep-dive. Quick notes from our side after a sync with ops:
- We will redact PII but keep distribution of prompt lengths and retrieval counts; aim to upload by 1/22 as Sasha noted.
- Procurement asks for an estimate of monthly committed spend for the pilot (range is fine) and contract term options (3/6/12 months). Ben — can you provide a conservative monthly estimate before the call so procurement has a number to react to?

Two small asks for the deep-dive agenda:
1) A short section on fallbacks — if Dedicated falls back to hosted variants, how is data isolation and request routing handled?
2) Confirmation of SLA targets for the pilot vs production (we want to tie the launch SLA to the Dedicated pricing).

Appreciate it — see you on the call.

Alex

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@jupiterai.com>, Sasha Lee <sasha.lee@jupiterai.com>, procurement@jupiterai.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-26T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: JupiterAI — post-call growth plan & pilot next steps

Alex / Sasha / Procurement team — thanks again for the productive deep-dive last week. Follow-up and concrete asks so we can move the SOW + procurement timeline along: 

Deliverables (action items):
- Redwood (Ben): conservative committed monthly estimate for the pilot (delivered via updated pricing sheet) — due 2026-01-27 EOD.
- JupiterAI (Sasha): upload anonymized prompt set + minute-level traces to the Drive link — due 2026-01-28.
- Procurement (procurement@jupiterai.com): send your preferred PO template and any specific audit/KMS requirements — due 2026-01-29.

Answers to the two asks from the call: 
1) Fallbacks and routing: Dedicated pools are fronted by Redwood’s smart routing mesh. If we detect capacity pressure we will transparently route eligible requests to compatible hosted model variants (policy controlled by you). Data isolation for Dedicated is enforced at the network and tenant layer; requests routed to hosted fall back to encrypted, ephemeral keys and logging with explicit audit flags — we’ll provide the architecture diagram in the SOW.
2) SLAs: Pilot SLAs will be operational targets (latency/uptime) with formal SLA tied to committed Dedicated capacity at production cutoff. We’ll include target numbers in the SOW, and suggest a 30-day performance review before switching billing model.

Proposed timeline: finalize SOW + pricing the week of 1/29, sign PO week of 2/5, pilot kickoff 2/15. If that works for procurement, we’ll run the 6-week pilot through 3/29 with a 30-day review and expansion decision by end of April.

If everyone is aligned I’ll convert the pilot scope into a SOW draft and share it for comment tomorrow.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
